issues.body:
Before this PR, parse_xsd_f32 delegated to parse_xsd_f64, so the xsd:float and xsd:double lexical acceptance sets were identical BY CONSTRUCTION. The new body re-implements the acceptance rule (the NaN / INF / +INF / -INF specials and the `is_ascii_digit() || +-.eE` byte filter) as a second copy in a different crate from sparq_core::parse_xsd_f64.

That shared body is explicitly documented as load-bearing. sparq-core/src/lib.rs states: 'This is load-bearing: the old raw str::parse::<f64> cache stored `inf` for "inf"^^xsd:double, which the evaluator type-errors - a cache MORE lenient than the evaluator.' That is the sq-9781x bug, and the single shared body is what closed it.

I verified there is NO wrong answer today: I probed the f32 and f64 FromStr paths over "1.", ".5", "1e400", "1e-400", "3.4e38", "1E2", "+1", "-0.0", "1e", "", ".", "+", "1.5E2" and the accept/reject decisions are identical, and cache_f64_seam_vs_as_numeric_differential still passes. The problem is that this parity is now maintained only by the two copies happening to match, and nothing tests it. The existing test only asserts three f32 cases (INF, -INF, nan), so an edit to either filter would drift silently and re-divergence would reach the sargable =/< fast path and the JKey::Num value join.

Note the value seam is deliberately unchanged and remains f64-based (cached_numeric_f64 returns parse_xsd_f64 un-narrowed for xsd:float), so this PR does not perturb the cache's stored value - the concern is purely the ACCEPTANCE predicate losing its single source of truth.
issues.fix_hint:
Preferred: keep one shared body. Add a generic or macro-shared acceptance helper in sparq-core, e.g. `pub fn xsd_float_lexical_kind(v: &str) -> Option<XsdFloatLexical>` (or a `pub fn is_xsd_double_lexical(v: &str) -> bool` plus the specials), and have BOTH parse_xsd_f64 and parse_xsd_f32 dispatch through it, differing only in the final `v.parse::<f64>()` vs `v.parse::<f32>()` and the special constants.

Minimum acceptable alternative: add an anti-drift differential test asserting `parse_xsd_f32(v).is_some() == parse_xsd_f64(v).is_some()` over a broad lexical matrix - reuse the existing bad-spelling list ("inf", "+inf", "-inf", "infinity", "-infinity", "Infinity", "nan", "NAN", "", "abc", "1_000", "0x1p4", " 1", "1 ") plus the good ones ("NaN", "INF", "+INF", "-INF", "6", "+1", "1.5E2", "-0.0", "1.", ".5") - and reference sq-9781x in the failure message so the invariant is self-documenting.
issues.title: parse_xsd_f32 duplicates sparq_core's XSD acceptance predicate, reopening the sq-9781x drift surface with no anti-drift test

issues.body:
This change alters documented public-API behaviour (parse_xsd_f32 is `pub`) and invalidates two statements that are still in the tree:

1. crates/sparq-substrate/README.md lines 60-61 say the shared lexical helpers are '(split_decimal, parse_xsd_f32/parse_xsd_f64, fmt_xsd_double; the parsers delegate to sparq_core::parse_xsd_f64 - one shared body with the core numeric cache, sq-9781x).' After this PR parse_xsd_f32 no longer delegates and there is no longer one shared body. The repo has an explicit public-API -> README/SKILL sync rule.

2. The module provenance block in the changed file (crates/sparq-substrate/src/numeric.rs, around lines 12-24) claims the move was 'behaviour-neutral' and that 'classification is bit-identical to what the engine did before the move.' That is exactly what this PR intentionally changes for xsd:float: on a double-rounding witness, as_numeric now yields a different f32 than the pre-move engine did. Leaving the claim unqualified is honesty drift in a file whose whole point is lexical fidelity.

Neither affects runtime correctness, but both are stale-claim issues rather than style nits.
issues.fix_hint: Update README.md lines 60-61 to describe the new split, e.g. 'parse_xsd_f64 delegates to sparq_core::parse_xsd_f64; parse_xsd_f32 shares the same XSD acceptance set but rounds directly at f32 precision to avoid double rounding (<bead id>)'. In numeric.rs, add one qualifying sentence to the provenance block noting that xsd:float classification deliberately departs from the pre-move f64-narrowing behaviour, since the pre-move path double-rounded, and cite the bead. Also consider naming the bead id in the new promoted_f32 doc comment for traceability.
issues.title: Two in-tree doc claims are now false: the 'parsers delegate to sparq_core' README line and the 'bit-identical to pre-move' provenance note

issues.body:
`Num::Dec(d) => d.lexical().parse::<f32>()` allocates a String on every Dec-operand-with-Float binop, where the previous `self.f64() as f32` was allocation-free. This only fires on the mixed decimal x float path (rank == 2 with a Dec operand), which is uncommon, and the accuracy gain is real: rounding the exact decimal lexical straight to f32 is correctly rounded, whereas going via d.f64() double-rounds. So the tradeoff is defensible and I am not asking for it to be reverted.

Flagging only because the repo carries a performance-dominance mandate and this is an allocation newly introduced into an arithmetic path. A related edge: Dec::lexical sizes its buffer with `String::with_capacity(mag.len() + scale + 2)`, so a Dec carrying a very large scale would allocate proportionally to that scale here.
issues.fix_hint: Optional. If the Dec x Float path ever shows up in a profile, compute the correctly-rounded f32 from (mant, scale) directly, or use a stack SmallString / write! into a fixed-size buffer (a Dec lexical is bounded by roughly 40 digits plus the scale) instead of the heap String. Worth a follow-up bead rather than a change in this PR.
issues.title: promoted_f32's Dec branch allocates a String on the arithmetic path

verdict.summary:
The core numeric fix is CORRECT and I verified it empirically. I independently reproduced the double-rounding witness: 4611686293305294849 as f32 = 0x5e800001 (correctly rounded) vs as f64 as f32 = 0x5e800000. So the new test is genuinely non-vacuous and goes RED on the pre-PR code. Routing Int/Dec/Double->f32 through a single rounding, and parsing xsd:float lexicals directly at f32 precision, is the right XSD/IEEE behaviour. The Dec branch's lexical round-trip is also strictly more accurate than the old d.f64() as f32, and its expect() is provably unreachable (Dec::lexical only ever emits [-]digits[.digits]). Test results: sparq-substrate 66/66 pass, sparq-reason green, sparq-engine green (exit 0, no conformance regression).

I am requesting changes on a structural regression rather than a present wrong answer. The new parse_xsd_f32 hand-duplicates the XSD acceptance predicate (the NaN/INF/+INF/-INF specials plus the ASCII byte filter) that previously lived in exactly one place, sparq_core::parse_xsd_f64. That shared body is documented in-tree as load-bearing: sq-9781x closed a real bug where the cache was MORE lenient than the evaluator, and sparq-core's own doc comment says so explicitly. I probed 13 edge lexicals and confirmed the two copies accept identically TODAY, so there is no wrong answer now. But the guarantee is now by coincidence rather than by construction, and no test pins the two acceptance sets equal (the existing test checks only INF/-INF/nan for f32). A future edit to one filter silently reopens the cache-vs-evaluator divergence surface.

Secondary: the change makes two in-tree doc claims false. Fixes are cheap and mechanical; no redesign needed.
